title: Stem Cell Therapeutic and Research Reauthorization Act of 2025
official_title: To reauthorize the Stem Cell Therapeutic and Research Act of 2005, and for other purposes.
likelihoodReason: Introduced by Rep. Christopher H. Smith (R-NJ-4) with 21 cosponsors and a cross-party original cosponsor group including Reps. Matsui (D-CA), Bilirakis (R-FL), Pingree (D-ME), Tenney (R-NY), and Mfume (D-MD). The House-passed measure now moves to the Senate. Short reauthorizations of the C.W. Bill Young Cell Transplantation Program have historically cleared both chambers by voice or unanimous consent — the most recent prior reauthorization (Public Law 117-15) advanced on that pattern — and the modest $2M-per-year increase in the primary authorization matches the profile that typically clears the Senate.

referencedSources.label: 42 U.S.C. 274m (Section 379B of PHS Act — C.W. Bill Young Cell Transplantation Program authorization of appropriations)
42 U.S.C. 274k (Section 379 of PHS Act — C.W. Bill Young Cell Transplantation Program) and 274k note (Cord Blood Inventory, from Section 2 of Stem Cell Therapeutic and Research Act of 2005)

summary: The C.W. Bill Young Cell Transplantation Program is a federally administered system, run by the Health Resources and Services Administration, that identifies, matches, and distributes bone marrow and cord blood units for transplantation for patients without a matched biologically related donor; the National Cord Blood Inventory (Section 2 of the Stem Cell Therapeutic and Research Act of 2005) contracts with qualified cord blood banks to build and maintain an inventory goal of at least 150,000 units of high-quality cord blood. This bill adds $33.009M of appropriations authorization for each of fiscal years 2027 through 2031 for the C.W. Bill Young Cell Transplantation Program on top of the existing $31.009M for FY2022 through FY2026, and extends the National Cord Blood Inventory authorization by striking "2026" and inserting "2031".
brief: Extends the C.W. Bill Young Cell Transplantation Program appropriations authorization at $33.009M per year through FY2031 and extends the National Cord Blood Inventory authorization through FY2031.

top_lines.headline: What the Program Does
subs: Identifies, matches, and distributes bone marrow and cord blood units for transplantation
Runs a national single point of access for transplant physicians and patients
Runs a patient advocacy and case management office
Recruits bone marrow and cord blood donors, with priority to underrepresented populations
Contracts with qualified cord blood banks to build the National Cord Blood Inventory (goal: at least 150,000 high-quality units)

top_lines.headline: Program Authorization Increased
subs: Existing $31.009M-per-year authorization for FY2022 through FY2026 preserved
Adds $33.009M for each of fiscal years 2027 through 2031
Effectively a $2M-per-year increase over the FY2022-2026 authorization

top_lines.headline: Cord Blood Inventory Extended
subs: Amends Section 2(g) of the Stem Cell Therapeutic and Research Act of 2005
Extends existing $23M-per-year National Cord Blood Inventory authorization through FY2031

sections.label: Section 2 — Reauthorization of the C.W. Bill Young Cell Transplantation Program

items.main: Adds a new authorization of $33.009M for each of fiscal years 2027 through 2031 to Section 379B of the Public Health Service Act (42 U.S.C. 274m), on top of the existing $31.009M-per-year authorization for fiscal years 2022 through 2026.
items.detail: The amendment restructures Section 379B by turning the existing single-figure authorization into paragraph (1) and adding a new paragraph (2) authorizing $33.009M for each of fiscal years 2027 through 2031. This is the appropriations authorization used to fund the HRSA-administered C.W. Bill Young Cell Transplantation Program described in Section 379 of the Public Health Service Act (42 U.S.C. 274k) — a $2M-per-year increase over the fiscal year 2022-2026 authorization.

items.main: Extends the National Cord Blood Inventory authorization by striking "2026" and inserting "2031" in Section 2(g) of the Stem Cell Therapeutic and Research Act of 2005 (42 U.S.C. 274k note).
items.detail: The referenced Cord Blood Inventory note currently authorizes $23M for each of fiscal years 2022 through 2026 to build and maintain an inventory goal of at least 150,000 units of high-quality cord blood through contracts with qualified cord blood banks. This bill's one operative amendment to Section 3 shifts the end year of that authorization from 2026 to 2031 without changing the dollar figure or the underlying contract, recordkeeping, or standard-of-care requirements.

gaps: The bill increases the C.W. Bill Young Cell Transplantation Program authorization by $2M per year but does not adjust the $23M-per-year National Cord Blood Inventory authorization for FY2027-2031, holding it flat.

The bill extends both authorizations through FY2031 but does not modify the 150,000-unit inventory goal set in Section 2(a) of the Stem Cell Therapeutic and Research Act of 2005, despite the intervening 20+ years of program operation.

The bill preserves the existing every-2-year state-of-the-science review under 42 U.S.C. 274k(o) but does not require any new report to Congress on new-cell-therapy inclusion tied to the FY2027-2031 authorization window.

The bill continues the underlying $30M contract-duration cap under 42 U.S.C. 274k(a) ("one or more contracts") but does not address the number of qualified cord blood banks required to meet the higher aggregate authorization.

featured_quotes.name: Mr. Smith
featured_quotes.text: Each year over 3.6 million babies are born in the United States. In the past, virtually every placenta and umbilical cord was tossed as medical waste. Today, doctors have turned this medical waste into medical miracles. Not only has God, in his infinite wisdom and goodness, created a placenta and an umbilical cord to nurture and protect the precious life of an unborn child, but now we know another gift awaits immediately after birth. Something very special is left behind: umbilical cord blood that is teeming with life-saving stem cells.

featured_quotes.name: Mr. Bilirakis
featured_quotes.text: Every year, thousands of Americans battling leukemia, lymphoma, sickle cell disease, and other blood disorders rely on the C.W. Bill Young program to help find a compatible donor. For many patients, that match is their only chance at survival, Mr. Speaker. This legislation reauthorizes the program, modernizes the National Cord Blood Inventory, and strengthens our Nation's transplant system to help ensure patients continue to have access to these lifesaving transplants.

featured_quotes.name: Mr. Pallone
featured_quotes.text: It is not only bipartisan, it is very important.

added: New Section 379B paragraph (2) of the Public Health Service Act (42 U.S.C. 274m) — $33.009M authorized for each of fiscal years 2027 through 2031
modified: 42 U.S.C. 274m — existing appropriation clause redesignated as paragraph (1) to accommodate the new paragraph (2)

Section 2(g) of the Stem Cell Therapeutic and Research Act of 2005 (42 U.S.C. 274k note) — authorization end year shifted from "2026" to "2031", extending the $23M-per-year National Cord Blood Inventory authorization through FY2031
